content_sections.title: Place an event in the past
content_sections.body_text: The past simple locates a completed event before now. Timeline: yesterday — RAN — now. Run changes to ran: ‘I ran home yesterday.’ Put a finished-time phrase with the event. Say run for now or a routine; say ran for the completed past event.

content_sections.title: Use run for movement
content_sections.body_text: Here run means move on foot faster than walking. Model: ‘Mai ran to the gate.’ Picture walking, then faster movement. Retell with ran plus one destination: home, the gate, or the station. Keep the movement meaning.

content_sections.title: Make a coherent help request
content_sections.body_text: A: ‘I ran here, but I cannot find Gate 2. Please help me.’ B: ‘Yes. Gate 2 is beside the café.’ A: ‘Thank you.’ Notice: the request names the needed help, and the reply provides it. Rehearse both roles, then change the gate number.

content_sections.title: Build syllables, then integrate
content_sections.body_text: Clap once for ran, twice for sta-tion, and three times for yes-ter-day. In help, finish /l/ then /p/ without an extra vowel; practise slowly, then as one syllable. Finally retell the past event and request help. Check: ran marks the past, run means fast foot movement, and the reply solves the request.
